settings.heroTitle: Adventure, friendship and the outdoors, on the edge of the Burren.
settings.heroLede: 7th Clare Scout Group in Ballyvaughan welcomes young people from 6 to 17. We camp, hike, build, cook, paddle and learn to look after each other and the wild places around us.
settings.about:
We're a volunteer-run Scout Group based in Ballyvaughan, County Clare, part of Scouting Ireland. Our programme is built around the Burren: limestone hills, the Atlantic on our doorstep, caves, green roads and dark skies.

Young people plan their own adventures with the support of trained adult leaders, gaining skills, confidence and a lasting love of the outdoors along the way.
settings.venue: Beavers and Cubs meet at the hall in Ballyvaughan. Scouts and Ventures meet at Newquay National School.

Bag-packing days, the annual quiz night and the Christmas raffle all need helpers and prizes. If you can give a few hours, donate a prize, or know a business that might sponsor a tent, email the group.

kits.title: Sionnach Adventure
kits.event: Two-night mountain expedition, patrols of four, Friday to Sunday
kits.summary: You carry everything for two nights on the hill: tent, food, water, cooking gear and clothes. One rucksack only, nothing carried in your hands, and no day bags. Pack light, pack dry, and pack it yourself so you know where everything is.
tips: Line your rucksack with a heavy-duty plastic bag (a compost or fertiliser bag is ideal) and put sleeping bag and spare clothes in their own dry bags inside it. Double waterproofing is the rule.
Heavy things go close to your back, middle to bottom. Light things on top. Waterproofs, map, compass, snacks and water go in the lid or side pockets where you can reach them.
The weight should sit on your hips, not your shoulders, and nothing should swing when you walk. Wear the packed bag at a meeting before the event and get a leader to help you adjust the straps.
Boots must be broken in over a few weeks. Runners and trail shoes are not allowed and you will be sent home.
Friday dinner is eaten before you leave or on the way. Plan for two breakfasts, two lunches and one patrol dinner.

kits.title: Mountain Pursuit Challenge (MPC)
kits.event: Weekend navigation challenge, teams of four plus a leader observer, Friday night to Sunday
kits.summary: MPC is navigation day and night through the mountains, fully self-sufficient. You carry everything: two nights of camping, food, water and cooking gear, and you will be walking in the dark on Friday night. The kit is the same as a Sionnach with more emphasis on light, torches, warm layers and being able to find things in your bag without unpacking it.
tips: Every item has a place in your bag and you know where it is with your eyes closed. Night navigation is where badly packed bags fall apart.
Two light sources per person: a good head torch on your head and a small backup torch in your pocket. Fresh batteries in both, spares in a ziplock.
Weight matters more on MPC than on any other event. Aim for a rucksack that is no more than a quarter of your body weight once shared kit is divided out.
You will camp late on Friday night. Have your sleeping clothes, mat and bag packed together at the top of the main compartment so camp takes ten minutes, not forty.
Practice route cards, pacing 100 metres, walking on a bearing and adding magnetic variation before you go. The observer cannot help you navigate.
